did_you_know.text: Did you know? Job describes controlling his gaze as a personal covenant: he committed himself not to look at a woman in a way that might lead him into sin.
Did you know? Job invites God to test him in the “scales of justice,” declaring that he is willing for his actions to be weighed fairly.
Did you know? Job denies not only committing adultery, but also harboring inner temptation or lying in wait at the door of another man’s wife.
Did you know? Job claims that he did not deny his male or female servants justice, grounding this in the fact that both they and he were created by God.
Did you know? Job presents his concern for the vulnerable as part of moral integrity: he mentions the poor, widows, orphans, and those without clothing, and denies withholding help from them.
Did you know? Job rejects using force against an orphan and even accepts a severe punishment if he had indeed raised his hand against one.
Did you know? Job declares that gold was not his security, distinguishing between wealth a person possesses and the absolute trust that belongs to God alone.
Did you know? Job mentions the sun and moon as examples of the temptation to worship the heavenly bodies, but denies that he kissed them or secretly worshiped them.
Did you know? Job declares that he did not rejoice over his enemy’s downfall or curse him by wishing for his death; at the same time, he describes his home as open to guests and strangers.

Did you know? At the end of his speech, Job asks to receive the written indictment, ready to wear it as a crown and answer every charge. He even accepts punishment if the land was harmed by his actions.
